cosy-lesson.title: Make Your Own Kind of Music

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Be yourself – To act naturally and authentically according to your own values rather than conforming to others' expectations.

p.em: Example: Cass Elliot urges listeners to embrace their individuality and be yourself even when walking alone.

cosy-blockquote.p: Late – Occurring or arriving after the expected, usual, or proper time.

p.em: Example: It is never too late to start making your own kind of music and choosing your own direction.

cosy-blockquote.p: Melody – A sequence of single notes that is musically satisfying; a tune.

p.em: Example: The song's uplifting melody stays in your mind long after the track finishes playing.

cosy-blockquote.p: Choir – An organized group of singers, especially one that performs together in concerts or church services.

p.em: Example: Singing in a choir brings people together, but sometimes you must stand out and sing your own tune.

cosy-blockquote.p: Chorus – A repeated section of a song that contains the primary musical and lyrical message.

p.em: Example: The powerful chorus reinforces the theme of remaining true to your personal path.

cosy-blockquote.p: Solo – A musical piece or section performed by a single performer.

p.em: Example: Taking a solo moment in life requires courage when everyone else is singing in harmony.

cosy-blockquote.p: Happy – feeling or showing pleasure or contentment.

p.em: Example: Listening to our favorite songs always makes us feel happy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Friend – kind and pleasant; behaving in a helpful or supporting way.

p.em: Example: The new neighbors gave us a very warm and friendly welcome.

cosy-blockquote.p: Path – A route, track, or course of action taken toward a specific destination or goal.

p.em: Example: Forging your own path can feel lonely at first, but it leads to genuine self-fulfillment.

cosy-blockquote.p: Harmony – The combination of simultaneously sounded musical notes to produce chords and a pleasing effect.

p.em: Example: Finding inner harmony allows you to navigate life's challenges with confidence and peace.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: There is a big improvement of → Correct: There is a big improvement in my English ((Use 'in' after 'improvement' to express domain.))
Incorrect: It was a great relief of → Correct: It was a great relief to hear the news ((Use 'relief' + infinitive 'to hear'.))
Incorrect: She is in the choir since → Correct: She has been in the choir for three years ((Use present perfect + 'for' to show duration of state.))
